edges.description: B-cell infiltration to the portal area is associated with serum IgM elevation and disease activity. The mechanistic relationship between B-cell recruitment and AMA production is unclear.

Serum alkaline phosphatase reports the cholestatic injury pattern caused by progressive small-duct loss in PBC; lower ALP is associated with longer transplant-free survival and is used with bilirubin as a composite surrogate endpoint in PBC trials.

Serum bilirubin reports impaired bile flow and cholestatic progression downstream of ductopenia in PBC; normal bilirubin is used with alkaline phosphatase response as a composite surrogate endpoint in PBC trials.

nodes.description: Autoantibodies against the E2 subunit of pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDC-E2) are highly specific for PBC. These antibodies may directly contribute to biliary epithelial cell damage through immune complex formation and complement activation. The origin and maintenance of AMA production involves complex interactions between genetic predisposition, environmental triggers, and dysregulated B- and T-cell responses.

evidence.reference_title: A contemporary perspective on the molecular characteristics of mitochondrial autoantigens and diagnosis in primary biliary cholangitis.
evidence.snippet: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is an autoimmune hepatobiliary disease characterized by immune mediated destruction of the intrahepatic small bile ducts and the presence of antimitochondrial antibodies (AMAs). The mitochondrial autoantigens have been identified as the E2 subunits of the 2-oxo-acid dehydrogenase complex, including the E2 subunits of pyruvate dehydrogenase, branched-chain 2-oxo acid dehydrogenase complex, oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex, E3 binding protein and PDC E1 alpha subunit.

evidence.reference_title: Current Landscape and Evolving Therapies for Primary Biliary Cholangitis.
evidence.snippet: Although the pathogenesis of the disease is multifactorial, there is a consensus that individuals with a genetic predisposition develop the disease in the presence of specific environmental triggers. A dysbiosis of intestinal microbiota is increasingly considered among the potential pathogenic factors.

readouts.interpretation: Serum bilirubin reports impaired bile flow and cholestatic progression downstream of ductopenia in PBC; normal bilirubin is used with alkaline phosphatase response as a composite surrogate endpoint in PBC trials.

nodes.description: CXCR5-mediated B-cell homing to the portal area increases B-cell infiltration and portal inflammation. The infiltrating population is enriched for IgM+ B-cells that express elevated CXCR5, correlating with disease activity. The relationship of B-cell infiltration to anti-mitochondrial antibody production remains to be determined: whether B-cell recruitment directly drives AMA production, is mediated by altered T-cell help, or reflects a consequence of prior immune dysregulation is incompletely understood.

evidence.reference_title: rs57494551 increases CXCR5 expression and IgM(+) CXCR5(+) B-cell infiltration in the portal area of primary biliary cholangitis.
evidence.snippet: The number of IgM+ CXCR5+ B-cells was increased in the portal area of PBC with high-disease activity.

nodes.description: The risk allele rs57494551 disrupts transcriptional repression at the CXCR5 locus, increasing CXCR5 expression on IgM+ B-cells. This elevation is measured by mRNA expression clustering and correlates with disease activity markers (serum IgM, AST, M2BPGi).

evidence.snippet: rs57494551 regulates endogenous CXCR5 expression in B-cells through binding to the transcription repressor TEA domain transcription factor 3 (TEAD3).

nodes.description: Destruction of bile ducts leads to ductopenia, impaired bile flow, and accumulation of toxic bile acids. Retained bile acids cause further hepatocyte damage and promote fibrosis.

evidence.reference_title: Role of the Gut-Liver Axis in the Pathobiology of Cholangiopathies: Basic and Clinical Evidence.
evidence.snippet: In recent years, several studies have shown that, in case of a change in gut bacterial homeostasis or impairment of intestinal barrier functions, cholangiocytes, which are the epithelial cells lining the bile ducts, activate innate immune responses against gut-derived microorganisms or bacterial products that reach the liver via enterohepatic circulation. Intestinal dysbiosis or impaired intestinal barrier functions cause cholangiocytes to be exposed to an increasing amount of microorganisms that can reactivate inflammatory responses, thus inducing the onset of liver fibrosis.

evidence.reference_title: Current Landscape and Evolving Therapies for Primary Biliary Cholangitis.
evidence.snippet: Bile acids are also recognized as playing an important role, both in disease development and therapy. Thus, while bile acid-based therapies, specifically ursodeoxycholic acid and obeticholic acid, have been the cornerstone of therapy in PBC, novel therapeutic approaches have been developed in recent years.
